newsitem.title: CHINA: China OKs Britain's consul in post-colonial HK.
newsitem.headline: China OKs Britain's consul in post-colonial HK.

text.p: China said on Thursday it had approved the appointment of Robert Francis Cornish, head of the British Trade Commission in Hong Kong, as Britain's first consul general in post-colonial Hong Kong.

The Chinese Foreign Ministry informed the British embassy in Beijing that it had approved the Queen's appointment of Cornish as Britain's consul general in Hong Kong after the crown colony reverts to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30, ministry spokesman Cui Tiankai told a news briefing.

Ye Minglang, an attach with the Chinese Foreign Ministry's Department of Consular Affairs, on Thursday presented a Beijing-based British diplomat with a document allowing Cornish to take up his post in Hong Kong after the handover, Cui said.
China agreed last September to allow Britain to set up a consulate in Hong Kong after the handover, Cui said. Britain informed China of its choice on June 13, Cui added.
On Monday, China said it had so far agreed to allow 84 countries, including the United States, to retain their consulates in Hong Kong after the handover.
There were 98 consulates in Hong Kong as of May 1.

It was not known how many consulates would not be allowed to stay on. China was still in the process of issuing documents to countries that would allow their consuls general to remain in the territory after the handover.
China has said countries that do not have diplomatic relations with it will not be allowed to maintain consulates in Hong Kong after July 1.
